contents.entry: Pointers: parent, siblings, DAG and principles
Shared needs: what the shared author declares for this node
Mechanism: one systemd user unit, one clock, five tick loops, one health answer
How it starts without an agent typing
Every wait, its timeout and its fallback
Retries up to 3, then recover and report
State paths and the cleanup script for each

pointers.sibling: JSON schema of unit.start in and tick, health out
pointers.principle: Rule 2 (no cog: N-06 owns the clock, nothing starts by an agent typing) and rule 7 (herdr is the owner's window; every system process is its own supervised unit)
The collision answer every node gives: leases with fencing tokens, compare-and-swap, idempotent steps, 409 that reports
pointers.needs: The shared anchors this volume relies on, declared as needs until shared/ lands
pointers.shared: Where this node goes live in the one cut-over order of the book

shared-needs.rule: shared/ belongs to the shared author (brief C, "What R-03 produces"); this volume never writes it and never points into it before it exists. Each need names the volume and the anchor the shared author declares. check.sh (N-46) resolves a need by volume and anchor once the shared volume lands, so a need becomes a live pointer without a hand edit. The same needs are returned to the shared author as data by the seat that wrote this volume.
shared-needs.need: Rows for unit.started 100; tick (subkinds scheduler, poll, backup, stall, health, daily) 100; health.recovered 200; reload.applied 200; tick.missed 500; unit.crashloop 500; unit.duplicate 500; reload.failed 500; health.unhealthy 503. Owner-acts: unit.crashloop; health.unhealthy with reason store, disk or crashloop; tick.missed at three in an hour; three watchdog restarts in an hour.
Entities tick:<subkind> (n, at, interval_seconds, class for backup) written by compare-and-swap once per tick; the tick record carries subkind, n, at.
Entity health:service (status, reasons[], counters, version, config_hash, at) and table health_history(at, status, reasons JSON) appended on transition; pruned by cleanup-logs.sh --health.
The system comes up before humans and agents; the unit is 100 percent operational and checked before the line is kicked (global rule: design first, system first).
Every wait has a timeout and a fallback; nothing starts by an agent typing; the clock is the only trigger.
The owner's always-on monitor never stops on a halt: ticks, health, backups, the poll and the push transport keep running under hold (memory rule bearings-stable-is-the-only-always-on-monitor).

tick intervals scheduler 5, poll 30, stall 15, health 15, backup 21600, daily 00:05Z; drain_seconds 30, reload_seconds 10, health.check_seconds 2, health.keep_days 30, logs.keep_days 14; env COQ_STATE, COQ_REPO, XDG_RUNTIME_DIR, the secrets file path.
Restart=always in 5 s, no start limit; unit.started with reason; three in ten minutes is unit.crashloop and one card; the unit keeps restarting because a dark line is worse than a noisy one.
A second binary started by hand: flock on STATE/run/service.lock refuses, exit 3, unit.duplicate 500 naming the holder pid.
WSL suspend and wake: tickers fire once each, the tick counter shows the gap, tick.missed once per subkind.

purpose.is: N-06 is the machine that starts the factory: one systemd user unit runs the one Go binary; the binary owns the one clock; the clock emits every tick the other nodes run on (scheduler, poll, backup, stall, daily); and the unit answers health for the whole service so monitoring is the system reporting on itself.

It is the root of the DAG's time: no node polls on its own timer and no agent starts anything; the system comes up before humans and agents, like starting the machines before the line is kicked (global rule: design first, system first).
purpose.is-not: It is not herdr: herdr is the owner's window only (D08, C46); no pane hosts this process, and no node calls herdr to schedule, route or store. It is not a container: the small cut runs the binary on the host under systemd (D22, C38), not in Podman.
purpose.decisions: D01, D08 (C46: every system process is its own supervised unit), D22 (C38), D09 (C41: small cut, keep interfaces and the fake clock), SPEC-16 sh-unit (one supervised unit, domain loops as goroutines) kept.

record.who: systemd --user, at boot through linger, on crash through Restart=always, or on `systemctl --user start coq-service` by the owner.
record.field: COQ_STATE, COQ_REPO, XDG_RUNTIME_DIR and the secrets file path; nothing else; every tunable is in scheduler/config/scheduler.json (SPEC-16 l-config kept: a missing key is exit 3 naming the key).

also.note: reload tables and config; the clock and the ticks are not restarted
read every tick; a hold stops dispatch and merges, never ticks, health or backups (bearings-stable-is-the-only-always-on-monitor: a halt never stops monitoring)

record.field: scheduler (tick.scheduler_seconds 5), poll (forge.poll_seconds 30), backup (backup.interval_seconds 21600, with class), stall (stall.tick_seconds 15), daily (tick.daily_at 00:05Z).
A per-subkind counter that only grows since start, with the start id, so a late or doubled tick is detectable.
record.rule: Ticks are entities, not log records: the entity tick:SUBKIND is CAS-written every tick (version grows) and broadcast in-process to the node loops; the records log gets only tick.missed 500 (a tick late by two intervals) and tick.daily 100, because 17,280 scheduler ticks a day in the log would bury every real record and flood N-31.

record.field: serving or not_serving, the grpc.health.v1 answer, plus the reason list when not serving.
store (N-01), forge (N-04 snapshot age), backup (N-05 age), leases (sweep age), ticks (every subkind's age), disk (free under STATE), unit (pid, started_at, version, config hash).
Every counter the six G1 nodes and the other service nodes expose, by name, reset at start (SPEC-16.I kept as the shape: counters live in the answer, no metrics server).
record.rule: health is an entity health:service CAS-written every health.tick_seconds 15 and pushed by N-31; the log gets health.unhealthy 503 and health.recovered 200 once per transition (latched), never per tick.

mechanism.component: scheduler/host/systemd/coq-service.service, installed by `make -C scheduler install-unit` into ~/.config/systemd/user/: Type=notify, ExecStart=%h/.local/bin/coq-service run (the binary make build wrote, copied by install), Restart=always, RestartSec=5, StartLimitIntervalSec=0 (never give up: a crash loop is visible in health history, and giving up is the 9.5 h dark outage of L06 section 5.2 again), WatchdogSec=60 (the binary sends WATCHDOG=1 every 20 s from the tick loop, so a hung loop is killed and restarted by systemd, never by a pane reader), TimeoutStopSec=drain_seconds plus 10, EnvironmentFile=%h/.local/state/coq/coq-jev-herdr-plugin/config/service.env, KillMode=mixed. `loginctl enable-linger` is a runbook step so the unit starts at boot with no login.

core.Clock (scheduler/internal/core/interfaces.go) with the real implementation returning time.Now().UTC() and testkit.Clock for tests; every node receives the clock by injection; nothing calls time.Now directly (go vet rule in lint: a grep for time.Now outside clock.go fails the build).

Package scheduler/internal/unit: one goroutine per subkind on a time.Ticker from the clock; each tick writes the entity tick:SUBKIND and sends on a per-subkind channel with a buffer of 1; a slow consumer coalesces ticks (level-triggered consumers do not need every tick, T03), and a consumer that has not drained in two intervals is reported tick.missed with the subkind.

grpc.health.v1.Health on the control socket XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/coq/control.sock (mode 0600) plus Status (the SPEC-16 Scheduler service shape: Health, Status, Reload, Drain, Retry kept on the same proto, generated code regenerated by `make proto` in the build container). Every check is a function returning ok or a reason with a bound of health.check_seconds 2; a check over its bound is a reason itself.
mechanism.mermaid: sequenceDiagram participant SD as systemd --user participant U as coq-service run participant ST as N-01 store participant T as tick loops participant H as health SD->>U: ExecStart (boot by linger, or Restart) U->>U: resolve STATE (state-root rule), load config (exit 3 on a missing key) U->>ST: open, quick_check, migrate (3 attempts) ST-->>U: SERVING or NOT_SERVING U->>U: recover: N-02 leases, N-03 claims, N-05 temps, flag backup:running U->>T: start scheduler, poll, backup, stall, daily loops U->>H: serve control.sock, store.sock U->>SD: READY=1 loop every 20 s T->>SD: WATCHDOG=1 end loop every 15 s H->>ST: CAS health:service, latched transitions to the log end SD->>U: SIGTERM U->>T: stop ticks U->>ST: finish in-flight, checkpoint TRUNCATE, close U->>SD: exit 0 within drain_seconds
mechanism.schedule: Scheduler 5 s, poll 30 s, stall 15 s, health 15 s, backup every 6 h with class tick, daily at 00:05Z (and backup class daily at the first backup tick after 03:00Z, monthly at the first daily of a month). All from config keys named in record.schema.json; a tick interval under 1 s or over a day is a config validation error at start.
mechanism.hold: The entity flag:hold (set by N-29 from a control.action or a card) is read into memory on every scheduler tick; N-07 and N-09 check it before any dispatch or merge; ticks, health, backups, the forge poll and the push transport keep running under hold, because the owner's monitor never stops on a halt.
mechanism.counters: Every node registers counters by name at start; Status returns them all; a reset at start is itself a counter (unit.restarts_total is read from the health history in the store, so it survives restarts).

start.rule: Nothing starts by an agent typing. systemd starts the unit at boot because linger is enabled; a crash is restarted in 5 s; a hang is killed by the watchdog and restarted. The owner's only hand action is the one-time install in the runbook.
start.step: Install once: `make -C scheduler install-unit` copies the binary to ~/.local/bin/coq-service, writes the unit file, runs `systemctl --user daemon-reload`, `enable --now`, and prints `loginctl enable-linger` if linger is off; the Makefile target is the one hand step and it is a script in the repository.
Start sequence as in the diagram; unit.started 100 with version, config hash, STATE path and reason; READY=1 only after the store is SERVING and the sockets listen.

A start that cannot open the store after 3 attempts still reaches READY=1 with health not_serving and reason store, so the health answer and the push to the owner's page work while the store does not (the monitor stays up when the line is down); N-28 raises one card.

The old bash watchers (route.sh, flow.sh, policy.sh, the five watch scripts) are not started by anything once this unit is enabled; N-49 and N-50 retire their units and cache copies (04-UNLANDED section 8).

wait.name: store-open
wait.fallback: READY with health not_serving; card; the unit keeps retrying the open every health tick so a fixed disk recovers without a restart

wait.name: tick-consumer
wait.on: a node loop draining its tick channel
wait.fallback: tick.missed 500 for the subkind; the tick is coalesced, never queued; health lists the slow subkind

wait.name: health-check
wait.fallback: the check reports timeout as its reason; the health answer is never blocked by one check

wait.name: watchdog
wait.fallback: systemd kills and restarts; unit.started reason watchdog; three watchdog restarts in an hour is an owner-acts code through N-28

wait.name: drain
wait.fallback: exit anyway; systemd's TimeoutStopSec kills at drain plus 10; the store's WAL makes that safe

wait.name: reload
wait.fallback: the old tables stay loaded; reload.failed 500 names the key; the ctl call returns the failure

retries.rule: Every automated step retries up to 3 times, then recovers and reports.
retries.step: 3 attempts at start, then not_serving and one card, with the open retried every health tick thereafter (recovery without the owner when the cause clears).

Restart=always with RestartSec 5 and no start limit; each start appends unit.started with reason; three crashes in ten minutes is unit.crashloop 500, one card, and the unit keeps restarting because a dark line is worse than a noisy one (L06 section 5.2: the dead man's switch never fired in a 9.5 h outage).
A CAS 409 on health:service (only possible after a restart overlap) is re-read and rewritten once; a store 503 skips this tick's write and the next tick writes.
A failed reload is reported and not retried by itself; the next `ctl reload` or SIGHUP tries again; the running tables are never half-replaced.

many-agents.reading: Every node, screen and seat reads one health entity and the tick entities through the store or N-31; the Status RPC is read-only and serves any number of callers concurrently.
many-agents.working: One process is the rule: the unit file's single instance plus a flock on STATE/run/service.lock taken at start; a second binary started by hand exits 3 with unit.duplicate 500 before touching the store, so two clocks can never tick one store.
many-agents.collision: A hand start while the unit runs: the flock refuses; the record names the pid that holds it.

systemd restarts the unit while a scheduler tick dispatches: the dispatch is a lease plus an idempotent Put (N-02, N-07), so the new instance's first tick finds the lease live and does not dispatch twice (level-triggered compare of open work with live runs).

The host sleeps and wakes (WSL suspend): the tickers fire once each, not once per missed interval (Go's Ticker drops ticks), the tick counter shows the gap, and tick.missed is reported once per subkind.

The owner sets hold during a tick: the flag is read at the start of the tick; a dispatch already past the check completes (it holds a lease and will finish); the next tick holds. Hold is a level, not an interrupt.

A dev or uat tier page idle-stops or stops unclean: N-06 counts the page.down (100 for a clean idle stop, 500 for a crash) on that tier's own lamp and in its restart counter; it writes no alert and no wake, and a STOPPED from a non-stable tier is a record, never a prompt to the architect (nodes/N-32/spec.xml#tier-rules, rule wake-only-stable). Only a stable-tier page.down 500 or watcher.dead 500 reaches the owner, as a card through N-28.
A reload swaps tables between ticks under a RWMutex; a tick in progress keeps the old pointer; the next tick sees the new.
many-agents.test: With testkit.Clock: 24 h of simulated ticks in under a second, with a suspend gap of 2 h, three injected crashes and two reloads: every subkind's counter is monotonic, exactly one tick.missed per subkind for the gap, health transitions appear once each in the log, and the lock refuses a second instance.

emits.acts: nobody; N-51 counts restarts in the day's audit
N-51 (exit test), N-05 (daily class), N-45 (timer cleanups)
nobody; N-43 reads the loaded hash
N-06 itself (health reason); owner card at three in an hour
the person who typed the second start; the record says so
the caller; the config ticket is wrong
owner through N-28 when the reason is owner-acts (store, disk, crashloop); otherwise the named node's own fallback

status-codes.rule: Every code above must exist in ../../shared/status-codes.xml#codes with the same meaning and actor.

path.cleanup: scheduler/host/bin/cleanup-unit.sh --apply: `systemctl --user disable --now coq-service`, remove the unit file and the binary copy; dry-run prints the three commands
scheduler/host/bin/cleanup-run.sh removes them when no live pid holds the lock; refuses otherwise
kept on purpose; listed in the README so cleanup-run.sh skips it by name; only the owner removes it, by break glass

path.writer: N-06 structured log (starts, ticks missed, health transitions, reloads)

path.cleanup: removed at drain; cleanup-run.sh removes a stale one
health_history rows older than health.keep_days 30 are pruned by scheduler/host/bin/cleanup-logs.sh --health
journald's own retention; `journalctl --user --vacuum-time=14d` is in cleanup-logs.sh --journal

out.record: health record whose status maps to owner-acts
health and hold state for the controls frame
daily tick for the exit test

also.note: in-group consumers; the drawn edges go through N-07 and N-12

item.check: The unit file has Type=notify, Restart=always, RestartSec=5, StartLimitIntervalSec=0, WatchdogSec=60, EnvironmentFile under STATE.
item.proof: `systemctl --user cat coq-service` saved in the test log; scheduler/host/tests asserts the keys.

item.check: READY=1 is sent only after the store is SERVING and both sockets listen.
WATCHDOG=1 is sent every 20 s from the tick loop; a blocked loop stops it.
item.proof: Test with a blocked loop and a captured NOTIFY_SOCKET: no ping after the block.

item.check: Every subkind ticks at its configured interval and the tick entity's version grows by one per tick.
A consumer slower than two intervals yields one tick.missed and coalesced ticks, never a queue.
health:service is written every 15 s and transitions appear once each in the log.
Hold stops dispatch and merges only; ticks, health, backup and poll continue.
item.proof: Integration test with flag:hold set: N-07 dispatch count 0, tick counters growing.

item.check: A second instance exits 3 with unit.duplicate.
item.proof: Script test starting the binary twice.

item.check: SIGTERM drains within drain_seconds and exits 0; the WAL is checkpointed.
item.proof: Script test; wal file size 0 after exit.

item.check: No time.Now outside the clock implementation.
Every state path above has its cleanup script, dry-run by default, registered in N-45.
item.proof: Each script run with no flags prints and exits 0; the registry lists them.

item.check: The unit starts at boot without a login.
item.proof: `loginctl show-user $USER -p Linger` says yes; a reboot test shows unit.started reason boot in the log.

actor.name: systemd --user
actor.may: start, stop, restart, watchdog-kill the unit

actor.name: N-06 in-process
actor.may: write tick and health entities, the lock and pid, notify systemd

actor.name: N-29, N-42 (code)
actor.may: set and clear flag:hold through a ruling or control.action record

actor.name: N-43 (code)
actor.may: call Reload after a status-code map commit

actor.name: seat (the model)
actor.may: `scheduler ctl health` read-only; never systemctl on this unit (the rendered seat settings deny it, N-13)

actor.name: owner
actor.may: install, enable, start, stop, restart; set hold from the Controls screen; break glass is the only path to stop the unit while the line runs, and the stop itself is recorded by the drain

monitoring.surface: The Controls screen (N-42) shows the unit as the reactor: running, hold, build-mode, watcher lamp, health reasons; the Map (N-38) shows the clock as the belt drive; Alerts (N-41) shows health.unhealthy, unit.crashloop, tick.missed. The bearings page (N-32) shows staleness from the health entity's age, so a dead unit is visible as a stale page within one health interval.

runbook.task: `make -C scheduler build` then `make -C scheduler install-unit`; run the `loginctl enable-linger` line it prints if needed; `systemctl --user status coq-service` shows active (running).
`scheduler ctl health` (the grpc.health.v1 answer plus reasons) and `scheduler ctl status` (counters, ticks, tables, held and dead jobs).
`journalctl --user -u coq-service -f` for the process; STATE/logs/service/*.jsonl for structured lines by node.
Merge the config ticket; `scheduler ctl reload`; reload.applied names the hashes.
From the Controls screen (N-42) or `scheduler ctl hold set --reason ...` (recorded as a control.action through N-29); `hold clear` resumes; ticks and monitoring never stop.
`systemctl --user restart coq-service`; the drain finishes in-flight Puts; leases survive (N-02 recover); nothing is lost.
`make -C scheduler build` then `make -C scheduler install-unit`, then restart; the version appears in unit.started.

item.what: every long-running process is a labelled herdr pane; the container runs in one, the executor in one
item.reason: C46 ruled herdr is the owner's window only and every system process is its own supervised unit; RC6 named one herdr server hosting everything as a root cause

item.what: the scheduler in a rootless Podman container with an executor on the host behind a unix socket
item.reason: the small cut (C41) runs one binary on the host under systemd; there is no herdr pane to type into, so the executor verb table has no job; builds and tests still run in Podman (l-make kept), the service does not

item.what: belt.file and belt.stale_seconds as the liveness signal; seat.busy_regex and seat.done_regex screen reads
item.reason: liveness is systemd's watchdog plus the health entity's age; screen regexes are K04 and V08 violations (an LLM screen is not a probe)

item.what: watchdog.timer as a separate dead man's switch unit
item.reason: item 10 is honoured by WatchdogSec in the same unit plus the bearings page staleness; a second unit that counts records was the one that never fired (L06 section 5.2); the exit test (N-51) is the outside-the-line timer that remains

item.what: ~/.cache/coq-watch/patrol-tick.sh and watchdog.sh as running line processes
item.reason: their probes are health checks here; the scripts are retired by N-49 under the LAND verdicts of WO-20261013-9617 and WO-20261013-bf70, which fold into this node

item.what: run.sh resolving the image digest and passing env into a container pane
item.reason: no container for the service; the digest pin survives for the pod images (N-22)

item.what: the Go service as a cluster pod (option C)
item.reason: C38 ruled test steps in pods and the service on the host; the store is a host file (SQLite does not work over a network filesystem)
